extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and extramural grant applicants (research community)
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement of NIH's simplified review framework for Research Project Grant (RPG) applications that reorganizes the five existing review criteria into three broader factors and describes how reviewers should score them to determine overall impact. Intended to guide peer reviewers' evaluation focus and scoring for grant receipt deadlines Jan 25, 2025 and beyond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1: Importance of the Research (Significance and Innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combines the prior Significance and Innovation criteria into a single factor assessing the importance of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This factor is scored on a 1–9 factor score. Reviewers should focus on whether the research addresses important problems and whether it represents meaningful innovation when assigning this score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2: Rigor and Feasibility (Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidates the prior 'Approach' criterion into a factor assessing the rigor, quality, and feasibility of the proposed methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This factor is scored on a 1–9 factor score. Reviewers should evaluate methodological rigor and feasibility when assigning this score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3: Expertise and Resources (Investigator and Environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combines the prior Investigator and Environment criteria into an assessment of whether the investigative team and institutional resources are sufficient for the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This factor is a binary assessment: rated either 'sufficient for the proposed research' or 'not sufficient'. If rated 'not sufficient,' reviewers must provide an explanation describing deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact Score
rubrics_metrics.description: An overall assessment reflecting the reviewers' judgment of the likely impact of the proposed research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will consider all three factors (Importance of the Research; Rigor and Feasibility; Expertise and Resources) when determining the overall impact score. The overall impact score summarizes the likely impact based on those factor assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (previous criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five current review criteria being reorganized; assesses the importance of the problem or critical barrier to progress being addressed by the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as part of the original five criteria (Significance, Innovation, Approach, Investigator, Environment) derived from NIH peer review regulations (42 C.F.R. Part 52h.8). Now incorporated under Factor 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (previous criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five current review criteria being reorganized; assesses whether the project challenges existing paradigms or employs novel concepts, approaches, or methodologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as part of the original five criteria and now incorporated under Factor 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (previous criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five current review criteria being reorganized; evaluates the proposed strategy, methodology, and analyses to accomplish the specific aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as part of the original five criteria and now represented by Factor 2 (Rigor and Feasibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator (previous criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five current review criteria being reorganized; assesses the qualifications, experience, and productivity of the investigators/principal investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as part of the original five criteria and now incorporated into Factor 3 (Expertise and Resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (previous criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five current review criteria being reorganized; evaluates institutional support, equipment, and other resources that contribute to project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as part of the original five criteria and now incorporated into Factor 3 (Expertise and Resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Central evaluative question: 'Can and should the proposed research project be conducted?'
rubrics_metrics.description: A framing question for reviewers intended to focus review on the key scientific and technical merits determining whether the project can and should proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The simplified framework is designed to better focus reviewers on this question; reviewers should use the three factors to address it when assigning factor and overall impact assessments.
